title: Anselm of Canterbury
speaker: Elder Scott Hollander

outline.title: Context of the Medieval Period
subpoints: Overview of the Middle Ages (476 AD - 15th Century)
Recognition of theological errors mixed with outstanding figures
The necessity of reform in the church

outline.title: Excursus on Lord's Day Worship
subpoints: Distinction between private/informal worship and corporate assembly
The ordinance of the visible church as the ordinary context for worship
Christ's command for gathering around Word, Sacraments, and Prayer

outline.title: Biography of Anselm
subpoints: Birth in Aosta, Italy, and contrast between pious mother and worldly father
Early spiritual inclination and departure from home
Education under Lanfranc at the Abbey of Bec

outline.title: Anselm's Theological Contributions
subpoints: Works on divine nature, free will, and original sin

outline.title: Historical Context: The Great Schism
subpoints: The 11th-century division between Western Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches
Excommunication of Pope Leo IX and Patriarch Michael I Cerularius

summary:
This session continues the Reformation series by examining the life and theology of Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, a pivotal figure in the medieval period. The speaker contextualizes the Middle Ages as a time of spiritual darkness yet highlights Anselm as an outstanding thinker who contributed significantly to philosophy and theology, particularly through his articulation of the ontological argument and his doctrine of the atonement. While acknowledging the presence of erroneous practices in the Roman church of that era, the study emphasizes the value of learning from these historical figures who represented important currents of thought.

A significant portion of the message is dedicated to an excursus on Lord's Day worship, prompted by a local debate regarding the validity of outdoor Bible studies as substitutes for corporate church attendance. The speaker argues that while private and informal worship is valuable, Christ has ordained the visible church as the ordinary context for the administration of the Word, sacraments, and pastoral shepherding. The distinction is drawn between the location of God's presence and the commanded structure of the gathered church.

The biography of Anselm covers his birth in Aosta, Italy, his difficult relationship with his worldly father, and his education under Lanfranc at the Benedictine Abbey of Bec. The session also touches upon the historical backdrop of the Great Schism, which permanently divided Nicene Christianity into Western and Eastern branches during Anselm's youth. The study aims to provide a balanced view of Anselm's legacy, recognizing both his intellectual brilliance and the theological limitations of his time.
